setups.name: Pullback in uptrend
setups.explain: A healthy stock (above its 200-day and with the 50-day above the 200-day average) has dropped 7–20% from its 20-day high and is oversold. Dips like this in strong stocks often bounce.

setups.name: Sharp 2–3 day selloff
setups.explain: A long-term uptrend stock just had a very sharp short selloff (2-day RSI under 5). These short panics frequently snap back within a week.

setups.name: Gap-down bought back
setups.explain: Opened at least 2.5% below yesterday's close, but buyers pushed it up through the day and it stays above its 200-day average — the drop may be temporary.

setups.name: Heavy-volume flush
setups.explain: Closed below its lower Bollinger band on 1.5x+ normal volume while still in a long-term uptrend — often a short-term capitulation low.

setups.name: Breakdown on volume
setups.explain: Closed below its 20-day low on heavy volume and is under its 50-day average. If you hold it, the trend says consider exiting.

setups.name: Overextended rally
setups.explain: Ran up too far too fast (14-day RSI above 78 and 12%+ above its 20-day average). Pullback risk is high — a good time to book some profit if you hold it.
